title: Micro-Compass: Mini-map Workspace Switcher with Contextual Cost Tiles
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Problem: Workspace switching in the Redwood Console currently requires a full modal or deep sidebar travel; customers running many projects report friction when trying to jump between environments while understanding immediate cost/rollout status. Goal: design a compact, keyboard-first "micro-compass" mini-map that surfaces 6–8 recent/favorite workspaces, quick actions (open, pin, switch role), and lightweight contextual tiles that show 1-line cost delta and primary rollout status. The component should be visible in the top-left corner of the console on wide viewports and collapse into a compact icon on small screens. This ticket drives the IA prototype, accessibility pass, and engineering handoff artifacts for the mini-map and the contextual cost tiles that integrate with the Console Dashboard cost lens and Rollouts panel.
acceptance_criteria: Micro-Compass prototype in Figma with interactive flows for open/switch/pin/quick-inspect
Cost tiles show live cost delta (24h) and high-level SLO impact tag (OK/Warning/Degraded) from telemetry mock
Keyboard shortcuts: Cmd/Ctrl+K opens the mini-map; arrows navigate; Enter switches workspace
Mobile fallback: micro-compass collapses to 'Quick Workspaces' sheet with same information
Handoff document with component specs, token usage, and accessibility notes uploaded to Confluence
design_decisions: Use progressive disclosure: show avatars + short name by default, reveal cost tiles on hover or via inspect action
Render cost tiles as single-line condensed chips with color-coded SLO badge to avoid visual noise
Prioritize keyboard navigation and ARIA roles over hover-only interactions to meet accessibility goals
Keep primary switch action immediate; pin/unpin and inspect are secondary contextual actions to reduce mistakes
Use existing left-rail compression pattern for narrow widths to avoid introducing a second competing rail
